name: Republic of Turkey

areaKm2.note: CIA World Factbook 1990: Turkey 780,580 km2 (low, mid). world_1960 Turkey polygon = 790,611 km2 computed by the pipeline (high).

population.note: OWID population (UN WPP) Turkey 1974 = 40,210,234 (mid, high). The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1974.shtml): 38,940,000 (low); COW NMC v7 tpop 1974 = 39,037k.

urbanization.note: World Bank SP.URB.TOTL.IN.ZS Turkey 1974 = 34.4% (low, mid). HYDE 3.5 via OWID (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/urbanization-last-500-years.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true): 42.56% (high). COW upop/tpop 1974 = 8,799/39,037 = 0.23 counts cities over 100,000 only.

activePersonnel.note: The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: total armed forces 453,000 (army 365,000, navy 40,000, air force 48,000) on 1 July 1974 (low, mid); Turkey added an estimated 20-30,000 men in Cyprus in July 1974 (same entry). COW NMC v7 milper 1974 = 574k (high, likely including part of the 75,000 Gendarmerie).

trainedReserves.note: The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: army reserves 750,000 (low), navy reserves 25,000 (mid, high = 775,000).

supportPersonnel.note: Active strength outside the P roles: army 365,000 minus ~155,000 infantry (infantry_line + infantry_light) = 210,000 (armour, artillery, engineers, signals, logistics); navy 40,000; air force 48,000 (The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru). 210,000 + 40,000 + 48,000 = 298,000 -> mid 290,000.

mobilizationRatio.note: Active 453,000 + 775,000 reserves (The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru) = 1.23M = 0.031 of 40.2M (low); + 75,000 Gendarmerie and recent conscript classes (mid 0.035); high 0.05 = 2.0M with older trained classes of the 20-month conscription.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Rifle strength of 12 infantry divisions, 2 mechanised infantry divisions, 3 mechanised and 5 infantry brigades (The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru) at roughly 7,000-8,000 infantry per division and 3,000 per brigade; many units below strength.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5 relative to 1974 NATO/Warsaw Pact best. Evidence: US-supplied Second World War and Korean War infantry weapons, SS-11 and Cobra ATGW, M-59 and M-113 APC in few units (The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 20-month conscription (The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru); NATO standards in the regular cadre; the July 1974 landing at Kyrenia was carried out against Greek Cypriot resistance (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_invasion_of_Cyprus).

count.note: Educated guess. Parachute brigade (The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru) and commando units; the Gendarmerie mobile brigades are not counted.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: light weapons and ATGW.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: selected long-service and conscript paratroops of the one parachute brigade (The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

count.note: The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 1,800 M-47 and M-48 medium tanks (low, mid) plus uncounted M-24, M-26 and M-41 light tanks and M-36 tank destroyers. High = The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1980.shtml): 3,000 M-47 and 500 M-48, suggesting the 1974 count is low. 160-180 M47/M48 went to Cyprus (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_invasion_of_Cyprus).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: M-47/M-48 of the 1950s against T-62 and M60A1 era best.

count.note: Educated guess. M-59 and M-113 APC listed without a count (The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru); The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1980.shtml): 2,000 M-113, M-59 and Commando (high); 150 M-113 with the Cyprus corps in 1980.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: M-59 and M-113 tracked APCs, no IFVs.

count.note: Educated guess. Guns and howitzers: The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru lists 105 and 155 mm SP guns and 105, 155 and 203 mm howitzers without counts. The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1980.shtml): 1,500 towed howitzers and 646 SP guns = 2,146 (high).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: US 105-203 mm towed and SP pieces of the 1950s-60s.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: NATO fire-control procedures.

count.note: The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: interceptors 28 F-5A and 30 F-102A = 58 (low); with the 33 F-104G of 2 fighter-bomber squadrons = 91 (mid); high adds the F-4 squadron at the 18-aircraft average squadron size given in the entry (109).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: F-104G and F-102A interceptors, F-4 entering service, against F-14 and MiG-23 era best.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: NATO-integrated air force of 48,000 (The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

count.note: The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 290 combat aircraft; fighter-bomber squadrons with F-4 (1), F-100D (5) and F-5A (2) = 8 squadrons x 18 (the entry's average squadron size) = 144 (mid); low 126 counts the F-4 squadron as forming; high adds 3 reconnaissance squadrons of RF-84F and RF-5A (54) = 198. 12 S-2E maritime patrol aircraft not counted.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: F-100D and F-5A dated; F-4 modern; unguided bombs.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: as fighters.

count.note: The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: army 20 AB-206 + 20 Bell 47G, air force 10 UH-1D + 10 UH-19D and some AB-204B, navy 3 AB-205A = 63 (low) plus the uncounted AB-204B (mid 70, high 80).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: light and utility helicopters, no attack helicopters.

count.note: The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 3 SSM battalions with 12 Honest John launchers (nuclear-capable under NATO custody).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: unguided Honest John rocket.

count.note: Nike batteries at 4-6 launchers per battery: The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru 2 SAM battalions with 72 Nike-Ajax/Hercules = 12-18 batteries (low 12). AA guns of 40, 75 and 90 mm listed without counts; The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1980.shtml): 900 40 mm guns = 150 batteries of 6 (high 15 + 150 = 165). Mid 100 assumes about half the 1980 gun holding plus 15 Nike batteries.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Nike-Hercules static sites and Second World War 40 mm and 90 mm guns; no mobile SAMs.

count.note: The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 14 destroyers (low, mid; ex-US Second World War types per The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1980.shtml)); high adds the 7 escort vessels.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Gearing, Fletcher and Sumner destroyers of 1943-45 (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1980.shtml)) without anti-ship missiles.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: NATO exercises in the Aegean and Black Sea.

count.note: The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 11 FPB, 27 MGB, 14 motor launches, 16 coastal and 4 inshore minesweepers and 8 minelayers = 80 (mid); low 58 without the motor launches and minelayers; high adds the 7 escort vessels (87). 90 landing craft not counted.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: gun and torpedo boats; missile FACs only from the late 1970s.

count.note: The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 15 submarines (ex-US Guppy and Tang types per The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1980.shtml)).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: modernised US fleet boats of the 1940s.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: NATO-trained staff planned and executed a joint amphibious, airborne and air operation and a second offensive that took 37% of Cyprus in August 1974 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_invasion_of_Cyprus); the first landing secured only a 3% bridgehead by the 22 July ceasefire.

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75 (national conscript army). Evidence: homogeneous officer corps with a strong Kemalist tradition; Kurdish conscripts in the ranks.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75 (motivated). Evidence: broad national support for the Cyprus operation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_invasion_of_Cyprus).

weapons.note: Anchor: 8 (1943) toward 9 (1985). Evidence: SS-11 and Cobra ATGW, US 105-203 mm artillery, Honest John (The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

armor.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: M-47/M-48 the best tanks; M-113 APC.

ships.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: 1943-45 US destroyers and submarines with post-war modernisation.

fortification.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: NATO hardened airbases and Straits defences.

logistics.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: motorised army, C-130 and Transall airlift (30 aircraft, The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

communications.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: NATO communications and air defence ground environment.

isr.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: RF-84F and RF-5A reconnaissance squadrons, S-2E maritime patrol, NATO radar.

air.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: F-4, F-104G and F-102A supersonic jets alongside F-100D and F-5A.

cyber.note: No military computer networks before ~1990 (cyber anchor 9 = 1990 networks).

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via OWID, Turkey: 1974 = 3.19% (mid; war year), 1975 = 5.12% (high, post-Cyprus build-up and US arms embargo); 1973 = 3.35%. Low = Global Military Spending Dataset (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/military-spending-as-a-share-of-gdp-gmsd.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) 1974 = 2.18% (1975 3.01%). The Military Balance 1974-75 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: defence budget 1974-75 $995M against 1973 GNP $21.5 bn = 4.6%.

industrialShare.note: World Bank NV.IND.TOTL.ZS Turkey (industry incl. construction, % of GDP): 1974 = 22.55% (mid), 1975 = 22.56%, 1973 = 23.7% (high).

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment (s = 1 assumed: Turkey was broadly self-sufficient in grain). World Bank WDI Database Archives SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS Turkey: 1975 = 64.8% (1989 Apr version; 65.7% in the 1999 Apr version) -> 0.35 (high); 1970 = 70.7% -> 0.29 (low); 1974 interpolated ~66% -> 0.34 (mid).

annualCohort.note: male population x 15-19 share / 100 / 5. World Bank SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN Turkey 1974 = 20,563,959 and SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y = 10.465% (https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/TUR/indicator/SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y?date=1974&format=json): 20,563,959 x 10.465 / 100 / 5 = 430,400 (mid); +-7% range.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. Patrol craft and landing craft from the Golcuk and Taskizak naval yards; missile boats came only with the Lurssen and Kartal programmes later in the 1970s (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Turkey entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1980.shtml)).

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook 1990: 49,615 km of highways (1985; high), of which 26,915 km bituminous (low). Mid 45,000 allows for growth 1974-85; village roads excluded.

railKm.note: CHAT railline Turkey 1974 = 8,141 km (low, mid); CIA World Factbook 1990: 8,401 km (high).

majorPorts.note: CIA World Factbook 1990: major ports Iskenderun, Istanbul, Mersin, Izmir (low, mid); high adds Samsun and Trabzon on the Black Sea.

merchantTonnage.note: GRT to DWT x 1.5 (low x 1.3, high x 1.6). CHAT shipton_all Turkey 1974 = 972 thousand GRT.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Motorised NATO-pattern logistics on interior lines; Cyprus supplied across a short sea crossing from the south coast.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules and donkeys in a country with ~65% of the labour force in agriculture; marginal for the army.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS stockpile series (OWID) lists no Turkish warheads. US warheads stored in Turkey under NATO nuclear sharing (Honest John, aircraft bombs) remained under US custody and are not counted.

basesAbroad.name: Kyrenia bridgehead and Nicosia enclave, Cyprus (from 20 July 1974)

chokepoints: Kars plateau and the Caucasus border

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: mountainous Anatolian interior, Straits and a nationally motivated population; low 1.1 for open Thrace, high 1.3 for eastern Anatolia.

notes: Snapshot date July-August 1974 (Military Balance 1974-75 data of 1 July 1974; invasion of Cyprus 20 July and 14-16 August per the Wikipedia article). NATO member with US equipment; the US arms embargo began in 1975. Region europe as in the other Turkey snapshots. Counts the entry gives only by type are bounded with the Military Balance 1980-81. Weakest values: the P-role split, APC and artillery counts, AA batteries (composite), roads in 1974 and animals (educated guesses or later-year bounds). Ship convention per SOURCES.md: destroyers ships_major (escorts in high); gun and torpedo boats, minesweepers and minelayers ships_minor; landing craft not counted.
